judgements.why: Both candidates come from the same draft, and the face regions are nearly identical (mean pixel difference 4.5 to 6.3 between them, against 14.5 to 21.5 from V13). FRONT, LEFT PROFILE, THREE-QUARTER and the full-figure head keep the V13 pose and bone structure: broad cheekbones, square jaw, straight nose, the same eyes and a thick curled handlebar moustache. The only changes are the intended removal of stubble, airbrushed skin and slightly heavier brows, so on both sheets every view reads as the same man as V13 and as each other, of the same apparent age. The newly drawn TURBAN head is a little narrower but still recognisably him. The deciding difference is that f1-2 still has the dark piercing dot on the LEFT PROFILE earlobe that fix1 item 3 asked to remove, and slightly more chin and jaw stipple. f1-1 has neither. Its tunic wrap runs opposite to the fix1 wording but matches the approved V13 sheet, so that is a prompt conflict rather than an identity error. Both candidates share failures worth a follow-up correction pass or a prompt caveat: the under-lip smudge in TURBAN, FRONT and THREE-QUARTER (a soul-patch risk), domed ball studs instead of tiny flat studs, and a LEFT FOREARM panel whose hand is drawn as a right hand. None of these changes the face, so f1-1 is the one to adopt for the identity lens.

judgements.why: On identity the two candidates are a tie. Their faces are almost pixel-identical, and both are clearly the V13 man in every view: same straight nose and bridge, broad cheekbones, square jaw, heavy-lidded almond eyes and long lean face. He reads leaner and older. The LEFT PROFILE is the closest match to V13, and all four large heads (main, FRONT, LEFT PROFILE, THREE-QUARTER) are consistently one man. Both share the same identity drifts. The brows are knitted into a heavier scowl, the moustache is fuller with tips that roll down where V13's hook up, and the small UNIFORM face is a little shorter and more generic, with no visible ear stud. The candidates differ only in hair and props. f1-2 has a wider silver band and a brown-highlighted topknot, and both push him past 'first grey at the temples' and away from the jet-black topknot. f1-1 has less grey and a darker topknot, so it is closer to the requested age and hair. Its faint X on the medallion and its glossy brand patch are small fixes that prompt caveats can cover (plain unmarked medallion; old flesh-toned scar). Adopt f1-1 with panel-prompt caveats on four points: a thin temple streak only, curls tied up, the stud always visible, and a clean-shaven chin. Do not adopt f1-2.

judgements.why: The two candidates are almost the same image. The faces, labels, costume and layout match, and all text is correct in both. Both also fail the same three points. First, fix1 item 2 was not applied: every head view keeps a broad silver sweep over the side of the head, not a thin first grey at each temple. That would push every chapter 17 to 28 panel toward the grey-streaked LATER LIFE look. Second, the UNIFORM figure has no ear stud. Third, the LEFT FOREARM panel draws a right hand, which could lead the panel generator to put the brand on the wrong arm. Both also show stubble-like stippling on the jaw. Between them, f1-2 is clearly closer. Its medallion is almost plain, while f1-1 has an embossed cross, which breaks fix1 item 4 and adds the cross motif the story avoids. f1-2's own extra fault is copper highlights in the topknot, which is milder. So no candidate should be adopted as is. f1-2 is the right base for a fix2 pass that thins the grey to temple streaks, makes the topknot jet black, adds the flush stud in UNIFORM, cleans the jaw shading, blanks the medallion sheen, and mirrors the forearm-panel hand to a true left hand.

judgements.why:
The two candidates are almost the same image. Pixel differences are confined to the three head studies and the BARE-HEADED head. The COURT figure and both bodies are effectively unchanged from V13, apart from slightly darker contrast on the COURT face and a bolder moustache.

On identity both pass. The FRONT study matches the V13 front face study closely: the same long straight nose with a rounded tip, the same brow line, the same moustache shape and thickness with upturned tips (measured dark area within about 13 percent of V13), the same pearl drops and the same apparent age of about 40. The LEFT PROFILE and BARE-HEADED faces read as the same man as COURT and as each other. The only real identity drift, in both, is expression: a knitted scowl with narrowed eyes instead of V13's calm deep-set gaze.

Neither candidate is better on identity, so the choice comes down to rule compliance. In both, the LEFT PROFILE and BARE-HEADED views put the knot on the upper back of the skull, which disagrees with the FRONT and BACK views where it sits on his left side. That is the main risk for panel generation. f1-2's knot sits slightly lower and nearer the ear in those two views, and its BARE-HEADED moustache is a touch tidier, so it edges f1-1. f1-1 has slightly darker, cleaner hair highlights.

Adopt f1-2 only with a panel-prompt caveat (the knot sits on the left side of the head above and behind the left ear, never at the back) and a calm-expression note, or run one more correction pass on the LEFT PROFILE and BARE-HEADED knots. Crops are saved under /tmp/claude-501/mv/.

judgements.why: The two candidates are nearly the same image: the pixel difference is confined to the three head studies and the bare-headed head. Both pass the hard rules. Labels are exact (MARTHANDA VARMA, COURT, BARE-HEADED, FRONT, LEFT PROFILE, BACK) with no extra text. Every view has pearl drop earrings and no stud. There is no crown, no beard and no forearm mark. The background is clean ivory. The BARE-HEADED figure looks to image left with the left ear showing, wears exactly two gold bead necklaces, the namam and a cream mundu with a narrow gold border, and is barefoot. The knot is on his left in FRONT (image right) and BACK (image left), and BACK has only one knot. Shared weaknesses: the LEFT PROFILE and BARE-HEADED knots sit on the back-top contour, so they read partly as a back bun; the COURT face drifted heavier than V13; FRONT looks older, with a moustache heavier than the 'neat, trimmed' spec; there is stubble shadow; and loose hair hangs behind the ear. f1-1 is the better pick because its hair carries fewer grey highlight strands in every view (f1-2's FRONT temple reads as silver-streaked, which breaks the strictest rule), its FRONT side hair is less wavy, and its BACK nape has no crossed twist that could read as a second roll. f1-2's only advantage is a slightly lower BARE-HEADED knot. Adopt f1-1, with prompt caveats for panels: 'knot on the left side just above and behind the left ear, never a back or crown bun; jet-black hair with no grey; neat, thin moustache; clean chin'.

The same warm brown skin tone, rendering and lighting
The same apparent age band, a mature man of about 35 to 45
Long black hair gathered into a knot when bare-headed (Ananthan Pillai's crown topknot, Varma's side knot), so the silhouette is a knot above or behind the head in both
Something in each earlobe (a gold stud for Nagoji, a pearl drop for Varma)
A lean, muscular, bare-chested build in the Kerala scenes
Both men turbaned in the formal panels (Nagoji's rust-red, Varma's cream-and-gold court turban), which hides hair texture, grey and knot placement and leaves only the face, the forehead and the ears
distinguishing_features: Forehead mark: Varma wears a white Vaishnavite namam with a red centre line, which still reads clearly as a pale vertical mark at 80 px. Nagoji's forehead is bare. This is the strongest single cue, but the bible asks for it only in the ch7 row.
Ear ornament: Varma has a large white pearl drop in each lobe, which shows as a bright dot at jaw level at 80 px. Nagoji's small gold stud is almost invisible at 80 px.

Hair texture and colour: Nagoji's hair is thick, curly and full, with a visible grey band at the temples from ch16 on. Varma's hair is sleek, straight and glossy jet black, flat to the skull, with no grey. This reads in bare-headed panels but is hidden under either turban.

Knot placement: Nagoji wears a large round knot high on top of the crown. Varma wears a small knot at the side, above his LEFT ear. This is clear in front and three-quarter views and weak in left profile, where both knots sit behind the head.
Moustache weight: Nagoji's is heavier and bushier, broad and drooping before it curls. Varma's is thinner and neatly waxed, with sharper upturned points. The difference is marginal at 80 px.
Face shape: Nagoji's face is longer and narrower, with hollow cheeks. Varma's jaw is slightly broader and squarer. This is marginal at 80 px and gone in greyscale face-only crops.
Build: Varma is drawn slightly broader through the chest and shoulders, Nagoji leaner. This is marginal and hidden in head-and-shoulders panels.

prompt_lines.varma: Marthanda Varma has a slightly broader, squarer jaw, a THIN neatly waxed moustache with sharp upturned points, SLEEK STRAIGHT glossy jet-black hair with NO grey, combed flat into a small knot at the side above his LEFT ear (never on top of the crown), a white Vaishnavite namam with a red centre line on his forehead, and a large white PEARL DROP hanging from each earlobe.

distinctness.verdict: Confusable. I cropped and compared the heads at 80 px and in greyscale face-only crops (saved under /tmp/claude-501/heads/). Under the hair and the ornaments, the two faces come from one template: the same long oval face, cheekbones, straight nose, dark handlebar moustache, clean chin, skin tone and age. The f1-1 sheets do separate them at 80 px, but only through features that can be dropped or covered: Varma's namam, his pearl drops, his straight black hair with no grey, and his side knot. A reader would lose the distinction in several situations. In the court-turban panels of ch10 to ch12, set beside Nagoji's rust-red turban, the faces are near twins, and only the namam and the pearl drops remain. The same happens in left profile, in Varma's white-headband scenes in ch11, in ch28, where he is aged and wears no jewels, and whenever the generator drops the namam. That last case is likely, because the bible asks for the namam only in ch7. The root cause is in the bible: Varma's base line names no facial features beyond "V13 varma-v1 face". It never mentions the namam outside ch7, the pearl drops, the straight hair or the absence of grey. Nagoji's line spells out the cheekbones, nose, thick curled moustache and grey temples, so the generator fills Varma's blank with Nagoji. The two prompt lines above should go into every panel prompt that shows both men. Exceptions for the namam and pearls (ch22 stitched brow, ch28 with no jewels) and any change to CONTINUITY.md need the author's approval, because CONTINUITY diffs need author approval.
